regions.text: かの那先比丘は深蘭に反間して「此等樹木何故不同』と云つた。

quote.translation: Nāgasena, whom we met earlier, put a question back to Milinda: "Why are these trees not the same?"

regions.text: 彌蘭はそれに對して「不同者本栽各異』と云つて比丘に答へまた自らに答へた。

quote.translation: Milinda answered the monk, and answered himself, by saying, "What is not the same is so because the original plantings each differ."

regions.text: しかしなから樹木の偶然性が因果律によつて苗の偶然性に移されたに止まつてゐる。

quote.translation: Yet in this answer the contingency of the trees has merely been transferred, by the law of causality, to the contingency of the seedlings.

regions.text: また「中阿含経」（巻四四、感成標）が「當知此業有。如是載也』といふときも。「成賞論」（参が「萬物従業因生』といふときも、恰かも偶然性に因果前説明を奥へたかの如くであるが、その實は低然性を無解決のまま原始偶然へまで無限に延長したに過ぎない。

quote.translation: Again, when the Madhyama Āgama (fascicle 44, the Parrot Sutra) says, "Know that this deed has such a retribution", and when the Tattvasiddhi (fascicle 10, chapter on the causes of deeds) says, "The ten thousand things arise from deeds as cause", it looks as though contingency has been given a causal explanation, but in reality contingency has merely been extended, unresolved, infinitely back as far as "primal contingency".

regions.text: かくて問題は假説的偶然の経驗傾域から離接偶然の形而上學的領域へ移されるのである。

quote.translation: The problem is thus transferred from the empirical domain of hypothetical contingency to the metaphysical domain of disjunctive contingency.
